Every life sciences company is racing to put AI into R&D. But commercial — the function that actually converts science into revenue — is still running on last quarter's call plans and static segmentation. Accenture and Wharton research estimates autonomous agents in commercial functions could unlock 6–10% in incremental global revenue. That's billions sitting in disconnected CRM notes, claims data, congress logs, field reports, and payer signals. Nobody's connecting them in time. This is the blind spot. AI investment flows where the science is. But revenue gets protected or lost where the customer is. The companies that close this gap will stop treating CRM as a place reps log calls and start treating it as the intelligence layer that connects field activity, medical affairs, market access, and real-world engagement signals. Not dashboards you check after the fact. A system that surfaces what's changing and what to do next before it hits the P&L. That's the design principle behind Exeevo's CRM platform on Power Platform. Commercial intelligence that's connected, compliant, and always on. The R&D AI revolution is real. The commercial AI revolution is overdue. #AgenticAI #LifeSciences #Pharma #MedTech #PowerPlatform #ExeevoCRM #HCPEngagement #CommercialStrategy #DigitalTransformation

Had a great time on the panel at the ProPharma event this week, alongside colleagues from ProPharma and Recordati , talking through where MI is heading in 2026 and beyond. A few things that stuck with me from the discussion: 🔹 MI is under real pressure to be faster and more accurate than LLMs. HCPs and patients are already using LLMs, whether we like it or not. 🔹 The winning formula isn't "standardise everything" or "personalise everything". It's standardise the science, personalise the delivery. 🔹 There are very mature AI use cases in MI today like translation and content creation. 🔹 Trust in AI doesn't come from the technology - it comes from curated data, human-in-the-loop review, and full transparency and auditability. 🔹 The biggest shift ahead isn't technological, it's strategic: MI is moving to a proactive insight partner doing work like flagging safety signals early, feeding medical affairs and pharmacovigilance in real time, and being measured on the decisions it influences, not just the enquiries it closes. Great energy in the room and some brilliant questions from the audience. Thank you to ProPharma for hosting, and to my fellow panelists ( Hannah Hunter , Victoria Evans . Emily Patel and Laura Avanzo Leeke ) for such a thoughtful conversation. #MedicalInformation #LifeSciences #AIinPharma #MedicalAffairs

Over the last two weeks I attended the Medical Information Leaders in Europe (MILE) Association meeting, followed by the International Social Pharmacy Workshop (ISPW). Whilst both events had different audiences and agendas, one common theme that emerged was that AI is an unavoidable part of healthcare. The focal question that resonated for me was “how do we harness AI while ensuring trust, scientific rigour and keeping people foremost?”. At the MILE - Medical Information Leaders in Europe meeting, discussions focused on how members of the public are increasingly turning to LLMs for medical information. Their ease of use and speed has propelled their adoption. However, they have been shown to generate inaccurate or misleading information with confidence. This highlights that Medical Information as a function needs to evolve not by choice but by necessity. One key challenge is meeting the expectations for rapid responses whilst ensuring that we continue to provide information that is accurate, evidence-based and trusted. At #ISPW2026 , one topic that particularly resonated with me was how AI can support research and extend the reach and impact of social pharmacy. I was particularly inspired by Prof. Kreshnik Hoti’s keynote on the first AI-powered pain assessment tool which was able to achieve an FDA De Novo approval, illustrating how AI can complement clinical decision-making when developed and evaluated rigorously. During my oral presentation, I had several engaging discussions about how I incorporated AI into thematic analysis. I shared how I used AI to augment qualitative thematic analysis while maintaining researcher oversight, transparency and methodological rigour. For me, these two events highlighted the same message from different perspectives. AI, when applied correctly, can amplify or augment but not without the appropriate expertise. If you're exploring similar questions around AI in healthcare, industry or academia, I'd love to hear your perspectives. A special thank you to everyone I met and caught up with over the past two weeks for the engaging conversations, and for enduring the European heatwave together. Today - I turn 50. It is the most productive year of my life and I wanted to share with you what changed. Work is fabulous, I'm in my best physical shape in decades, and home life is happy. At 49 It was the opposite - so I had to change things up. There is a saying that "you are the average of the 5 people you spend time with" so I wanted to be around others that have mastered their craft in search of some of the secrets to their discipline. So I spent a week this year living with Free diving Champion Davide Carrera (133 Meter Record Holder) and recently with Navy SEAL Commander Jimmy May (CEO of Mayday Executive Training and Chairman of the Board for Beyond The Brotherhood ) to see what it is that makes top performers tick. The experiences of living in these two households was like night and day yet had similarities worth sharing. Both households wake up before 5 am. They believe in hard work and they don't burn daylight. Every day has a goal to achieve and therefore deep focus and discipline. Why? If you spend time around these two masters, you will discover that they have deep PURPOSE. For Jimmy it is his patriotism, for Davide it is his message for respecting the oceans. What I found is that their hard work ethic is due to their strong sense of purpose. Spend a minimum of an hour with these two and some topic about the oceans or patriotism will come up. So tactically, you can wake up at 5 am too. You can work hard too. But a strong sense of purpose will separate the top 1% from the other 99%. So I realized in my 50th year that the one thing that I should focus on is not being more disciplined. Its about expanding my own sense of purpose. Here is the formula I worked out: First comes purpose. Through purpose you have meaning. Through meaning, you have discipline. Through discipline you have action. Through action you have results. This is what I learned from living with masters of their craft this year. So what's your purpose? Five years ago, I set out to fulfill a personal ambition and bridge a vital gap: to combine decades of corporate experience with rigorous academic credibility. Yesterday, that journey came full circle as I officially graduated with a Doctorate Degree in Business (GDBA) from Durham University Business School and emlyon business school 🎓 My research focused directly on the intersection of my professional passion and industry need: Examining whether shared leadership can drive R&D effectiveness within the Life Sciences sector. Navigating a highly rigorous doctoral program while stepping completely out of my comfort zone—tackling advanced statistics, presenting at academic conferences, and defending a 3-hour viva—was immensely challenging. But the ultimate goal was always clear: to blend academic theory with practical application to help shape the future of leadership in the sector where I have built my career. Achieving a lifelong ambition like this is never a solo effort. I am incredibly grateful to my supervisor, Susanne Braun , for pushing my boundaries with incredible support and inspiration, and to my brilliant family. Balancing my final corrections alongside a new job, while my three daughters were simultaneously studying for their SATs, GCSEs, and A-Levels, is an experience we will never forget. My biggest thank you is to my amazing wife who took my ambition and made it her own and never made me feel guilty for all the previous family time I had to sacrifice. To my network: never underestimate the power of purpose. Combining deep professional practice with academic validation has equipped me with the tools to better support the next generation of leaders and learners. The journey of lifelong learning continues! 🎉 #DUCongregation #ExecutiveLeadership #LifeSciences #DBA #BusinessResearch #SharedLeadership #ContinuousLearning

A brand that crushed it this week is Kraft Heinz . Their “Look Familiar?” campaign didn’t even show a ketchup bottle. Just photos of fries from restaurants around the world that happened to look like the Heinz label. No logo screaming at you. No explanation. You just get it. What I realized is that the strongest brands don’t need to introduce themselves—you already know who they are. When your brand is so recognizable that people connect the dots on their own, you’ve already won before they hit the grocery aisle. It’s a reminder that branding isn’t just about getting attention. It’s about sticking in people’s minds. It’s Simple. It’s Clever. It’s a perfect example of why consistency is so powerful in marketing.
